cards.back: A weighted sum of signals: keyword match, meaning match, recency, field and business rules each give one number per document, and you tune only the weights.
score = alpha·dense + (1 − alpha)·bm25. alpha = 1 is pure vector search and alpha = 0 is pure keyword search.
BM25 is unbounded while cosine sits in a narrow band, so a BM25 of 18 beside a cosine of 0.84 wins every sum unless you normalise first.
(s − min) / (max − min), per query and per list. One outlier squashes the rest, and near-ties get stretched to 0–1.
RRF(d) = Σ wᵢ / (k + rankᵢ(d)), with k = 60 by default. It uses ranks only, so no normalisation is needed.
A small k makes the #1 slot in either list dominate. A large k flattens the curve, so documents that do well in both lists win.
recency = 0.5^(age / half_life). With a 90-day half-life, a 90-day-old doc gets 0.5 and a 180-day-old one 0.25.
Filters remove, boosts reorder. Filter when the question pins a value; boost for a preference. Permissions are always filters.
Grid search on 100–300 labelled queries, sweeping alpha 0 to 1 in 0.1 steps, scoring NDCG@10 or recall@k on a held-out split.
After any signal change: a new embedding model, chunker or BM25 analyser moves score distributions.
Past a handful of signals, train a model (often LambdaMART gradient-boosted trees) on labelled pairs to learn the weights and their interactions.

quiz.q: You add raw BM25 scores to raw cosine scores. What happens?
choices: Cosine wins because it is closer to 1
BM25 wins nearly every query because its scale is larger
quiz.why: BM25 is unbounded, so it dominates unless scores are normalised.

quiz.q: With alpha = 0 in alpha·dense + (1 − alpha)·bm25, what is the search?
quiz.why: alpha weights the dense term, so 0 leaves only BM25.

quiz.q: Why do most engines ship RRF as the default hybrid mode?
choices: It always beats every linear blend
It uses the raw score gap between results
quiz.why: RRF ignores raw scores and uses only ranks.

quiz.q: Using a 90-day half-life, what recency value does a 180-day-old filing get?
Why is recency as a hard filter a failure mode?
choices: Last year's document vanishes when it is the only answer
quiz.why: Recency should be a soft decay, not a filter.

quiz.q: You swapped the embedding model. What should happen to alpha?
choices: Re-tune it on the labelled set
quiz.why: A new model changes the cosine distribution, so the best alpha moves.

quiz.q: How should user permissions be applied in scoring?
quiz.why: Permissions are always filters, never boosts.
